speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To begin my assessment, please describe exactly when these symptoms started and if they are constant or intermittent.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest is very characteristic of a neuromuscular junction disorder; can you tell me if you experience any droopy eyelids or difficulty swallowing? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The positive Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test, combined with your symptoms of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and specific double vision, confirms the diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis. Do you have a history of thymoma or other autoimmune conditions?
